name: Attacking 3-4-3 Wing-Back

slots.why: A high line leaves space behind the defence, so the keeper needs to claim through balls early and distribute quickly.
Wide centre-back who defends the channel the wing-back has vacated. The Cover alternate lets him sit behind a more aggressive partner.
Ball-playing defender in the middle starts build-up and passes through the opposition's press.
Wide centre-back on the other side, covering the space left by the right wing-back. Cover is the alternate if he is the safer of the two.
Attacking wing-back supplies the width, so the whole shape depends on him getting up the pitch and back again.
Mirror of the left side: with two wing-backs pushed on, the front three can play narrower and closer to the striker.
Box-to-box midfielder covers the ground the wing-backs leave and supplies the runs that support the counter-press.
Deep-lying playmaker sets the tempo and keeps the ball moving so the back three can push up.
Winger stays wide and beats his full-back, giving the attack a wide threat to go with the inside forward.
Inside forward cuts in from the right to shoot and attack the far post, overloading the box with the striker.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence. Poacher is the alternate for a striker who is better as a finisher than a runner.

description: A front-foot back-three system with wing-backs stretching the pitch and a front three occupying the back line.
whyGood: Three defenders permit aggressive wing-back positions and five-lane attacking occupation.
whyThisShape: Three centre-backs behind two attacking wing-backs put five players across the width of the pitch in attack and three forwards against a back four. The price is the space behind the wing-backs, so it only works while you keep the ball high up the pitch and win it back fast.
whenToUse: When you are clearly the stronger side and expect the opponent to sit deep, or you need goals late. It needs wing-backs with real stamina and centre-backs who can defend wide areas.
whenNotToUse: Against quick counter-attacking sides that target the space behind your wing-backs, or if your centre-backs are slow or your wing-backs tire before the hour.

instructionRationale.Much Higher Line of Engagement: Starts the press in the opponent's half, so the wing-backs' advanced positions are backed by pressure on the ball.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Keeps the back three close to the midfield and the team compact; it needs pace in the centre-backs.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Keeps possession inside the triangles the wing-backs, midfielders and forwards form.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Three centre-backs are a natural build-up base and draw opposition forwards out of position.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Wins the ball straight back after a loss, before the space behind the wing-backs can be attacked.
